title: Sandustry Tips — 20 Habits for Cleaner Early Access Factories
description: Sandustry tips checklist: dig discipline, filters, overflow, saves, fluids, performance, community sources, and beginner FAQ.

paragraphs: Dig for a goal (space, resource, fluid control), not for dopamine tunnels.
Keep the dig face narrow enough that you can still see logistics behind it.
Do not undercut belts and machines without a save.
If a cave is flooding, stop digging and fix fluid routing first.
Place filters before you think you need them.
Separate dig → buffer → refine → sink even in a tiny starter base.
Leave walkways and rebuild lanes — pixel bases get entombed.
Give overflow an intentional dump so clogs do not become mysteries.
When stuck, watch one junction for 30 seconds instead of adding more machines.
Isolate slag / residuals from the valuable path early.
Treat wet sand as a designed early loop, not a random weather event.
Learn one clean pipe/pump path before branching a fluid maze.
More sand rarely fixes a flooded belt.
Snapshot or save before terraforming under critical belts.
Use the demo to profile your PC before a long EA session.
Bookmark Steam news and the official wiki for patch-sensitive numbers.
Join Discord or Reddit for layout screenshots — not as a substitute for reading tooltips.
If a guide invents exact ratios without sources, ignore it during EA.
Automate the step you hate clicking first.
Stable flow beats bigger holes.
Rebuild in slices, not rage-wipes, when possible.
Write down the bottleneck in one sentence before redesigning.

faq.a: Automate the step you hate clicking first. Everything else is decoration until flow is stable.

faq.q: Best tip when the factory “randomly” stops?
faq.a: Watch the junction and the sink. Full outputs and unsorted merges cause most sudden freezes.

faq.q: Best tip before watching a megabase video?
faq.a: Make sure your own dig → buffer → refine → sink line already runs. Videos skip early sorting pain.
